2.name: Time Series
2.sub: Line charts, seasonality, calendars and motion

questions.prompt: Election night 2024: the exit poll's most important issue, drawn the way it ran on TV. What kind of chart is this?
questions.source: NBC News national exit poll, 2024 general election, most important issue (as shown on air): https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2024-elections/exit-polls

questions.prompt: Same chart: one nominal variable (the issue) and one quantitative variable (the share). Which encoding channels carry them?
options: Issue: color. Share: angle and area
questions.source: NBC News national exit poll, 2024 general election, most important issue (as shown on air): https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2024-elections/exit-polls

questions.prompt: The Democratic ticket went from 306 electoral votes in 2020 to 226 in 2024. What kind of chart tells that story here?
options: A bar chart of separate totals
questions.source: National Archives, Electoral College results 2020 and 2024: https://www.archives.gov/electoral-college/2020 https://www.archives.gov/electoral-college/2024 and Census 2020 apportionment: https://www.census.gov/data/tables/2020/dec/2020-apportionment-data.html

questions.prompt: You have two values: the Republican ticket's electoral votes in 2020 (232) and 2024 (312). Which chart fits better?
options: Either: they say the same thing
questions.source: National Archives, Electoral College results 2020 and 2024: https://www.archives.gov/electoral-college/2020 https://www.archives.gov/electoral-college/2024 and Census 2020 apportionment: https://www.census.gov/data/tables/2020/dec/2020-apportionment-data.html

questions.prompt: International airline passengers per year, 1949 to 1960. From this chart alone, what can we conclude?
options: It grew by the same amount every year
questions.source: Box and Jenkins airline passengers, R datasets::AirPassengers: https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/datasets/html/AirPassengers.html

questions.prompt: Indeed job postings in Ohio, 2022 only. They climb into spring, then fall. Does this chart show seasonality?
options: No: one year cannot show a pattern that repeats each year
Yes: the line goes up, then down
No: an index cannot be seasonal
questions.source: Indeed Hiring Lab, Job Postings on Indeed in Ohio (IHLIDXUSOH), via FRED: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/IHLIDXUSOH

questions.prompt: A calendar plot of traffic crashes per day in Cincinnati, 2025 (darker = more). Which pattern does it show best?
questions.source: City of Cincinnati Open Data, Traffic Crash Reports (CPD), unique crashes per day: https://data.cincinnati-oh.gov/Safety/Traffic-Crash-Reports-CPD-/rvmt-pkmq

questions.prompt: A motion chart of 142 countries, 1952 to 2007: income, life expectancy, population, continent. What is time mapped to?
options: The animation: each frame is a year
questions.source: Gapminder data via the gapminder R package (Bryan): https://cran.r-project.org/package=gapminder

questions.prompt: 2024 presidential results: each of the 3,153 counties is filled with the winner's color. What kind of map is this?
questions.source: County results compiled by Tony McGovern: https://github.com/tonmcg/US_County_Level_Election_Results_08-24 and county outlines from the Urban Institute's urbnmapr: https://github.com/UrbanInstitute/urbnmapr

questions.prompt: Same map: red covers about 85% of the land shown. What share of the national vote did the red candidate get?
questions.source: County results compiled by Tony McGovern: https://github.com/tonmcg/US_County_Level_Election_Results_08-24 and county outlines from the Urban Institute's urbnmapr: https://github.com/UrbanInstitute/urbnmapr

questions.prompt: Each Ohio county's 2024 margin runs from Harris +32 to Trump +69, and 0 is a tie. Which color scheme fits?
options: Map B: sequential, light to dark
Map C: diverging, two hues from a middle
Any of them: color is color
questions.source: County results compiled by Tony McGovern: https://github.com/tonmcg/US_County_Level_Election_Results_08-24 and Ohio county outlines from the Census cartographic boundary file: https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/cartographic-boundary.html

questions.prompt: Barley yields at six Minnesota sites, 1931 vs 1932, both years in one panel per site. At five sites 1931 beat 1932. Which site flipped?
questions.source: Immer, Hayes and Powers (1934), as lattice::barley; Cleveland, Visualizing Data (1993): https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/lattice/html/barley.html

questions.prompt: Weekly COVID cases per 100,000 by Ohio county, six snapshots as small multiples. Compared with animating the same maps, small multiples are better at:
options: Comparing dates side by side, without remembering frames
questions.source: ISA 401 course data covid_cases_county.csv (the Class 18 and 19 file), Ohio counties by week; county outlines from the Census cartographic boundary file: https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/cartographic-boundary.html
